San Mateo on Ice: Holiday Tree Lighting and Opening Event - Friday, November 13
Event Description:
The City of San Mateo and the San Mateo United Homeowners Association invite the San Mateo community to a magical tree lighting ceremony and the opening celebration of San Mateo on Ice. 
Enjoy a performance by Peninsula Skating Club figure skating performers: Olympic skater Polina Edmunds; National skater Sarah Zhang; rising stars Alain Sandraz, Lily Sun, and Maria Yang; the ice dance team, Jeffery Chen and Layla Karnes; and the Nazareth Ice Oasis Production group. San Mateo on Ice will officially open to the public on Saturday, November 14th and will be open daily (including holidays!) through Sunday, January 10th.

Visit the Family Farm and come face-to-face with miniature cows, playful goats, friendly donkeys, and more! 
Immerse yourself in a charming world of holiday cheer, where the historic House and Garden are beautifully transformed for the season. Then venture into the Redwoods where Thistlewyck, a whimsical Christmas village nestled under the towering trees, has shimmered back into view for all to enjoy.
NEW THIS YEAR: Explore the Filoli Family Farm where you will get to meet mini cows, goats, sheep, a mother donkey along with her baby, and more cute friends.
Daytime admission is FREE for members.*
 Member Holiday Daytime Tickets
 General Holiday Daytime Tickets

Calendar and Pricing
Introducing the Filoli Family Farm
Meet the Newest (and Cutest!) Residents of Filoli!
An all-new experience nestled within the fanciful world of Thistlewyck Village. Come face-to-face with miniature cows, playful goats, friendly donkeys, and more! Get up close, discover their personalities, and enjoy magical moments together that your family will be talking about long after the holidays.
The best part?
 It's all included with Holidays Daytime admission, and admission is FREE for Filoli members! 
From November 14 through January 3, make Filoli Family Farm part of your family's new holiday tradition.
Thistlewyck Village
 A spectacular daytime tradition.
Follow the trains into Thistlewyck Village, an expanded festive world tucked beneath the redwoods, with more family activities, holiday surprises, and seasonal fun included with admission.
Add a Thistlewyck passport at checkout for more seasonal fun
!*
Members get an extra perk: Thistlewyck Village will open exclusively for members from 9–10am, before opening to all guests.
Thistlewyck Passport
Looking for a little extra Holiday magic?
The Thistlewyck Passport guides you through the Thistlewyck Village and lets you collect your passport stamps along the way. Also included is an Elf Hat from the Elf Academy, a Train Toy from Thistlewyck Station, a cup of the World’s Best Hot Chocolate, and special stickers to boot! 
Tickets: $25; purchase as an add-on to your Holiday Daytime Admission 
Members receive 10% off
The Historic House for the Holidays
 A spectacular daytime tradition.
See Filoli at its festive best. Wander through the Historic House filled with 42 decorated trees, garlands, and holiday details inspired by Filoli’s historic connection to Muckross House in Ireland.
Across the estate, more than 200 real Christmas trees add to the celebration, including a magnificent 18-foot Nordmann fir in Woodland Court.
Members can start the magic early: the Historic House will open exclusively for members from 9–10am each day.
Explore Thistlewyck
Long ago, deep within Filoli’s misty redwood forest, fairies and woodland creatures created a magical railway to carry stories and holiday cheer across the land. Wherever the train stopped, tiny villages sprang to life, and hidden beneath Filoli’s towering trees was one of the most enchanting of all: 
Thistlewyck
. For generations, the village remained hidden from human eyes, but the wonder of children and the spirit of the holidays have brought its magic back into view. Now, Thistlewyck welcomes families to discover its tiny trains, festive cottages, playful elves, and woodland surprises.
Add to your Daytime Magic!

IlluminOdyssey 10
 10 years. 10 new exhibits. One glowing holiday journey into the science of light. 
Day
Hour
Minute
Second
 IlluminOdyssey is back! Catch the light: November 14, 2026 – January 24, 2027 
Reserve Your Tickets
Plan Your Visit
CuriOdyssey members get free admission to IlluminOdyssey during general admission hours. Please show a photo ID at the admission window to acquire member tickets, no reservation necessary. 
Learn more about membership at CuriOdyssey >
 IlluminOdyssey 10 
Inspired by the science of light, IlluminOdyssey is an immersive, interactive installation that will mesmerize kids and adults of all ages*. CuriOdyssey's four-level Redwood Hall will transform into a glowing forest of science—light your way through a maze of luminous botanical geometry, play with rainbow refraction and swirling projections, paint with light on phosphorescent surfaces, and dance with your shadow. Explore the physical properties of light, such as photoluminescence, color, additive light mixing, waves, fluorescence, fluid dynamics, subtractive color mixing, and refraction.
IlluminOdyssey is celebrating 10 years the only way we know how: bigger and better than ever. This milestone year brings 10 new glowing exhibits packed into Redwood Hall, with beloved favorites alongside dazzling new additions. This fan-favorite exhibition is free with admission or membership. CuriOdyssey's hands-on approach to science education influences every facet of this exhibition. IlluminOdyssey's interactive glowing exhibits awaken kids' curiosity, build critical thinking skills, and inspire an interest in science and the natural world. As a non-profit outdoor science museum and zoo, we make exploring science, technology, engineering, art, and math fun and exciting for kids and adults of all ages.
*Please note:
 This is a darkened hall with a variety of light-based exhibits and artwork. Visitors sensitive to light and sound may be affected.
 Glow Into Winter Break 
Keep curious kids shining while school’s out! Our full-day winter camps for ages 6–10 dive into bioluminescence, phosphorescence, reflection, and all things radiant, celebrating IlluminOdyssey’s 10th year. Pick a day, or come back for all three themes: Glowing Galaxy, Luminous Life, and Create and Illuminate.
Register Now
 Help Light the Way 
Every glowing exhibit in IlluminOdyssey starts with a supporter like you. Sponsor an exhibit and help spark wonder for thousands of kids and families this winter, from light-painting walls to shadow-dancing stages. Your gift brings hands-on science to life and keeps curiosity shining bright all season long.
Become a Sponsor
 Your Party, Lit Up 
Birthdays, weddings, holiday parties: every celebration glows brighter at IlluminOdyssey. Book our four-story Redwood Hall and let your guests explore a dazzling world of interactive light and color. Ask about our holiday events package.
Plan Your Event
 IlluminOdyssey 10 FAQ 
What is IlluminOdyssey 10?
IlluminOdyssey 10 is an indoor, interactive winter light exhibition for families at CuriOdyssey, a nonprofit science museum and zoo in San Mateo, California. It runs 
November 14, 2026–January 24, 2027.
 For its 10th year, CuriOdyssey's four-level Redwood Hall becomes a glowing forest of science, with 10 new exhibits alongside favorites from past years.
Is IlluminOdyssey okay for kids with sensory sensitivities? 
IlluminOdyssey is a darkened hall with light-based exhibits, and some areas have flashing lights and sound, which may affect visitors sensitive to light and sound. Sound dampeners and sensory tools are available at CuriOdyssey's front desk, and staff can help find a sensory-safe space. CuriOdyssey also hosts quarterly Sensory Sundays with fewer crowds; preregistration is required.
Is IlluminOdyssey educational? 
Yes. Every IlluminOdyssey installation explores how light works, including color mixing, refraction, fluorescence, photoluminescence, waves, and fluid dynamics. CuriOdyssey designed it to spark kids' curiosity and build critical-thinking skills through play, so it's both a holiday outing and a STEAM activity.
What age is IlluminOdyssey best for?
IlluminOdyssey is designed for kids and works for toddlers through tweens, and adults enjoy it too. For older kids, CuriOdyssey offers winter break day camps for ages 6 to 10, with themes inspired by IlluminOdyssey's 10th year.
What's new for IlluminOdyssey's 10th year?
IlluminOdyssey 10 adds 10 new glowing exhibits to mark its 10th season, alongside returning favorites. Families can expect a maze of luminous botanical geometry, rainbow refraction, swirling projections, light-painting walls, and shadow-dancing stages. IlluminOdyssey first opened at CuriOdyssey in November 2017.
When is IlluminOdyssey 10? 
IlluminOdyssey 10 runs November 14, 2026 through January 24, 2027 at CuriOdyssey, 1651 Coyote Point Drive, San Mateo, CA 94401.
What are IlluminOdyssey's hours?
During IlluminOdyssey, CuriOdyssey's winter hours are 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM daily, with last entry at 4:00 PM. 
How much are IlluminOdyssey tickets?
IlluminOdyssey 10 is included with CuriOdyssey general admission; no separate ticket is needed. Admission is $29.95 for adults (18–61) and $24.95 for children (18 months–17 years), students with ID and seniors (62+). Infants under 18 months and CuriOdyssey members get in free.
Are there discounts?
Yes. Families with EBT, SNAP or WIC get free admission through Museums for All. Military get 50% off with ID, and teachers get in free with a valid teacher ID. Reciprocal members of ASTC, AZA and ROAM may also qualify. Discount tickets are sold only on site, on the day of your visit.
Do I need to reserve tickets in advance?
Reservations aren't required, but we recommend reserving online. All tickets are for a specific date and time, and booking ahead cuts your wait. Members don't need a reservation; just show your photo ID at the admissions window.
What's the least crowded time to visit?
CuriOdyssey is busiest from 10 AM to noon. For a calmer IlluminOdyssey visit, come after 2 PM. Tickets have no time limit, so you can stay until closing.
Do members get special access?
CuriOdyssey members get free admission and free parking. Members are also invited to Member Mornings with breakfast, 8:30– 9:30 AM on November 21, 2026, and January 23, 2027 (RSVP required).
What else is there to do at CuriOdyssey?
IlluminOdyssey admission also includes CuriOdyssey's indoor science center, zoo, walk-through aviary, Nature Play Grove, Nature Play Garden, Bay Gallery and Whooosh! playground.
Is there an indoor holiday light show in the Bay Area for a rainy day? 
Yes. IlluminOdyssey 10 is fully indoors in CuriOdyssey's Redwood Hall in San Mateo, so rain and cold don't affect it. It runs daily from November 14, 2026, to January 24, 2027, with some holiday closures. CuriOdyssey's indoor science center is open the same day, so you can make a full visit without going outside much.
What are the best holiday light experiences for families in the San Francisco Bay Area? 
IlluminOdyssey 10 at CuriOdyssey in San Mateo is one of the Bay Area's top holiday light experiences for families with young children. It runs November 14, 2026–January 24, 2027. Unlike outdoor light walks and drive-thru shows, it's indoors, open during the day, and hands-on: kids touch, move, and play with the light. It's included with regular museum admission.
What's a good holiday light show for toddlers and preschoolers near San Francisco?
IlluminOdyssey 10 at CuriOdyssey in San Mateo works well for toddlers because it runs in the daytime, so the visit fits around naps and early bedtimes. Little kids can walk a glowing maze, dance with their shadows, and paint with light on glow-in-the-dark surfaces. Children under 18 months get in free. CuriOdyssey is just off Highway 101 in San Mateo, about 20 miles south of San Francisco.

Step inside the studios of 23 artists to see what they are creating, hear about their process and find art to bring home. Explore painting, photography, sculpture, textiles, printmaking and more as you make your way through the E, F and U wings at the north end of Cubberley Community Center.
Held twice a year, Open Studios invites you to meet the artists of the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, which supports artists with rent-subsidized workspace and a creative community in exchange for public programming and community service.
Come early for the book sale and lunch, then spend the afternoon exploring the studios and an interactive art installation.

Learn How to Build an Owl Box
Sunday, November 15, 2026
Presentation at 2 pm; Doors Open at 1:30 pm
Please join the Woodside Environment & Open Space Committee’s Autumn Event on how to keep 
Woodside Pesticide Free
 by learning more about how to build an Owl Box and attract owls to your property!
Adult barn owls typically consume 3 to 4 rodents per night (such as mice, voles or small rats) although some species or brooding parents can catch up to 10 to 12 rodents per night when feeding chicks!
About the Speaker:
Our guest speaker, John Gallagher, has built many owl boxes for his property and neighbors. He will take us through the easy step-by-step process of building an Owl Box and you will receive a link for instructions on how to build your own box.
John will help us learn more about owl habitat as well as their benefit in reducing the rodent population through his incredible photos of owls and owlets gathered on his property on the west side of Danville.
John is a long-time member of the Board of Directors of Save Mount Diablo, the land trust that works to conserve land around Mount Diablo and the rest of the Diablo Range. John manages some of the camera traps on land trust properties and has thousands of photos of local wildlife. 
Pesticide Free Woodside:
Come and join us to learn more on how to encourage owls to nest in your yard so you can avoid the use of poison to keep the rodent population in check. Visit the Environment & Open Space Committee's 
Pesticide Free Woodside
 section for additional resources!

Join Midpen partner, Latino Outdoors on Sunday, November 15 from 9am to noon for their Take a Hike Day at La Honda Creek!
One of Midpen's largest and most diverse preserves, La Honda Creek offers immersion into a historic ranchland with grazing cattle, views of the San Mateo County Coast and Santa Cruz Mountains and pockets of redwood forest.
The purpose of Take a Hike Day is to encourage people to step outside, enjoy local parks or nature trails, and experience the physical and mental health benefits of hiking.
The trail we will hike is around 3 miles with 300 ft in elevation gain, generally considered easy/moderate.
We will have tamales for folks and other snacks!

Saturday, November 14, 2026
10:00 am - 2:00 pm
 Skyline Ridge Preserve
Approximate Total Miles

Image
 Hike
Give thanks to Native Californians by exploring how they cared for the land since time immemorial before the arrival of settler-colonialists. Join Docent Naturalists Marie Faust Evitt, Nancy Weintraub, and Ann McCarty for a moderately-paced hike along the beautiful Ipiwa, Alpine Loop, and Sunny Jim trails. You’ll observe grassland, chaparral, and riparian habitats while discovering how local Native tribes use strategies such as cultural burning and regular pruning to nurture plants and ensure abundant food and materials for homes, baskets, and medicine. Children who can comfortably hike more than four miles are welcome. Bring a snack for a break at Alpine Pond.
 Where to Meet
Meet at the 
Skyline Ridge Circle Parking Area 
on Skyline Boulevard located one mile south of the Skyline Blvd. (Highway 35) and Page Mill/Alpine Road intersection. After entering the preserve, turn right and go to the farthest parking area. Those traveling from I-280 on Page Mill Rd. should allow approximately 45 minutes travel time.
